UX-01.criteria: Setup intro and form are separate; guide reference is not a working help link; avoidable invalid submission clears secret fields.

UX-02.criteria: Full portal navigation appears while sign-in is incomplete.

UX-03.criteria: Admin reads require ten-minute fresh MFA; missing assurance is presented as generic forbidden access. Groups have an independent equivalent check.

UX-04.criteria: Browser-session authentication and factor freshness are conflated.

UX-05.criteria: Registration → verify link → verify page/button → success page → Continue; permanent manual account-status link.

UX-06.criteria: A global continuation remains in the session rather than being consumed as a particular flow completes.

UX-07.criteria: The same Overview route substitutes a different welcome page.

UX-08.criteria: Repeated empty states, competing next actions, and misleading all/owned/shared state.

UX-09.criteria: Type-first creation, useful detail hierarchy and journal terminology are inconsistent.

UX-10.criteria: Sharing displays three empty projections and page-one footers; some role guidance is wrong.

UX-11.criteria: Normal validation errors can lose identity/navigation; only some forms receive complete editable recovery.

UX-12.criteria: Empty export uses generic wording and green success treatment.

UX-13.criteria: Selected client is lost through generic pagination; one-time password and detailed setup instructions are separated.

UX-14.criteria: App-password and recovery-code generation lack server-enforced same-intent replay protection.

UX-15.criteria: Security copy conflates configured protection and recent verification; adjacent security forms/confirmations need consistency.

UX-16.criteria: Standalone portability navigation duplicates resource context; successful preview/confirm render from POST despite a GET report route.

UX-17.criteria: Accounts filter mixes enabledness with sign-in method; handoff is incomplete; self/last-admin disable can lock out the operator.

UX-18.criteria: Group renaming dominates membership work; generic confirmations and messages are inaccurate for some states.

UX-19.criteria: Audit renders database codes/UUIDs as primary content. Native-app removal has no adequate final consequence confirmation.

UX-20.criteria: Admin overview contains outdated bootstrap wording and duplicate navigation. Diagnostics need clearer interpretation, not fabricated metrics.

UX-21.criteria: Guide, screenshot manifests and packaging checks encode obsolete flows; journal/restore documentation has drifted.

A01.criteria: Fresh setup at root and /team: operator command, valid code, account creation, PRG to login, no auto-login/passkey; legacy setup URL remains safe.
A01.observation: Operator issuance, trusted HTTPS setup, sign-in redirect and preservation of the legacy setup entry were exercised at the root and /team.

A02.criteria: Setup mismatch, invalid username, Unicode/code-point/byte limits, expired/replaced code, five failures, concurrent claims and rollback: correct form recovery and one permanent initialization winner.
A02.observation: The browser corrected a password mismatch without clearing the form. InitializationIT exercised malformed usernames, Unicode password byte limits, five failures, code replacement and expiry, both concurrent claims and transaction rollback.

A03.criteria: Setup never reopens after account disable/delete, restart, upgrade or restore; OIDC cannot provision the first administrator before protected initialization.
A03.observation: Initialization and OIDC boundary tests ran. Both upgrade and restore retained the closed initialization latch.

A04.criteria: Primary-only, registered-but-unverified and completed sessions: proper shell and direct-URL handling; no protected authority before accepted assertion.
A04.observation: Primary-only, registered and asserted sessions were exercised using accepted WebAuthn signatures. Incomplete sessions exposed the authentication shell.

A05.criteria: First sign-in invokes one registration and one explicit assertion; returning sign-in invokes one assertion; no duplicate Verify page or final Continue page.
A05.observation: First sign-in progressed through registration and one explicit assertion to Overview. Returning sign-in used one assertion.

A06.criteria: Cancel/timeout/unavailable API/provider/expired challenge/network uncertainty: accurate messages, focus, retry and authoritative outcome reconciliation; no false success or duplicate registration.
A06.observation: The browser exercised registration cancellation and reconciled a genuinely committed registration with an intercepted response. HTTP and unit tests exercised challenge validation.
A06.remaining: Exercise provider/API unavailability and expiry messaging in actual browsers and authenticators.

A07.criteria: At 9:59, exactly 10:00 and 10:01: ordinary authorized metadata navigation works in a completed session, sensitive admission preserves the existing strict freshness boundary for BOTH factors. New assertion alone does not rejuvenate stale primary.
A07.observation: Typed factor and session tests separate factor freshness from completed browser access.
A07.remaining: Record the completed-session metadata and both factor decisions at 9:59, 10:00 and 10:01 together in a controlled-clock browser or HTTP fixture.

A08.criteria: Thirty-minute idle/eight-hour overall boundaries and explicit Stay signed in: server enforcement, no background keepalive, no refreshed factor time, no overall extension from page views. Test actual overall reauthentication.
A08.observation: BrowserSessionTest tested the exact eight-hour proof deadline and a removed authenticating credential.
A08.remaining: Record production idle, explicit extension and end-to-end browser reauthentication at overall expiry.

A09.criteria: Disabled account, stale epoch, revoked session, removed authenticating key, removed last key, wrong-account key, forged/future factor evidence: fail closed with safe recovery. No old proof survives key removal.
A09.observation: Signed HTTP WebAuthn rejected cross-account, forged and disabled credentials. Factor and browser-session tests checked future evidence, revocation, epoch changes and the original live key. The browser removed the last key and denied sensitive actions until new enrollment. Restore rejected the previously live cookie.

A10.criteria: Real Keycloak authentication/linking, allowlist, managed-account restrictions, verified auth_time, outage, disabling and recovery: existing boundaries preserved; no local fallback or upstream role escalation.
A10.observation: Real Keycloak browser and HTTP profiles exercised allowlisted subject mapping, linking, fresh upstream auth_time, outage and disablement. The final browser rerun passed code recovery and re-enrollment while preserving local-password fallback and upstream role denials.

A11.criteria: Anonymous safe continuation, authenticated draft, fixation rotation, two tabs, changed account, expired/evicted intent and unsafe next values: proper binding, single consumption, no cross-account leakage or POST replay.
A11.observation: AuthenticationJourneyTest exercised path validation, session rotation, independent handles, rejection of replay and changed accounts.
A11.remaining: Verify simultaneous JDBC-session writes, same-handle contention and eviction across actual browser tabs.

A12.criteria: OAuth continuation with encoded redirect/state/PKCE at root and /team: legitimate request preserved; external/path-prefix/encoding/auth-loop attacks rejected.
A12.observation: Root and /team path validation, OAuth boundary and continuation tests ran.
A12.remaining: Retest the complete encoded OAuth authorization request with a browser at both deployment paths.

A13.criteria: Freshness expires while editing: only safe fields return, original version conflict preserved, new CSRF, real reauthorization, explicit resubmit; passwords/codes/uploads are not retained.
A13.observation: Safe form drafts are route- and account-bound and require a GET review before resubmission.
A13.remaining: Exercise stale version plus fresh CSRF in a real browser and cover every supported draft route.

A14.criteria: Shared layout survives ordinary 400/409 errors for all covered forms; active section/object identity preserved. Revocation/outage error paths never restore unauthorized metadata.
A14.observation: Invalid sharing preserved the signed-in shell. HTTP form tests exercised field associations and retained safe values.
A14.remaining: Exercise every browser-facing form and its revocation and outage paths. The follow-up test covered the oversized multipart form and header paths.

A15.criteria: Overview for initial admin, ordinary empty, shared-only, owned-only and mixed accounts: one page identity, useful next action, no mandatory personal collection, no stale-auth “unprotected” claim.
A15.observation: One Overview identity was observed for the initialized administrator and a shared-only account. A shared-only account can proceed without creating an owned resource.
A15.remaining: Record the ordinary-empty, owned-only and mixed next-action choices and stale-auth text as explicit assertions.

A16.criteria: Lists at 0,1,50,51+ rows, no-match, nonzero empty page, long/hostile names, all scope/filter combinations: accurate states, bounded queries, context-preserving pagination.
A16.observation: HTTP tests exercised bounded isolation, row recovery, search and paging. The browser exercised All and Shared scopes.
A16.remaining: Cover every scope/filter combination and all exact edge counts in the revised UI.

A17.criteria: Calendar/task/journal create and edit: type choice, optional fields, six/eight-digit color including alpha/empty values, fixed component type, unchanged identities, XSS resistance and stale writes.
A17.observation: Calendar, task list and journal creation, metadata and color paths exercised type labels, stable identifiers, escaped text and stale writes. Clients exercised the calendar color and content round trips.

A18.criteria: Owner/read-write/read-only/unrelated admin: controls and backend permissions agree. No private content/metadata access from admin role alone.
A18.observation: HTTP tests exercised owner, writable and read-only recipient actions, DAV permissions and role separation. Signed-in sharing controls matched scoped access in the browser.

A19.criteria: Sharing empty/direct/group/overlapping/disabled cases: correct effective access, precise removal result, ordinary-user directory privacy, admin group guidance and stale/concurrent grant behavior.
A19.observation: Direct, group and overlapping effective access have an authoritative backend projection with separate pagination.
A19.remaining: A signed HTTP regression checks that a same-count grant permission edit invalidates membership review before mutation. Dedicated final review is still missing for some grant revocations.

A20.criteria: Connections per supported client, no resources/shared-only, existing password/new password, root/subpath and selected-client paging/error/step-up: actual correct settings with secret and instructions together.
A20.observation: Client-specific setup and a one-time secret were shown together and worked in both clients. HTTP exercised authorized resource context through paging, validation recovery and issuance, and denied cross-account access.
A20.remaining: Record a completed browser step-up with the optional resource and rerun the native GNOME flow where its graphical dependencies are available.

A21.criteria: Same-intent app-password/recovery-code double-click, sequential replay, browser refresh, concurrent requests, rollback, commit response loss and expiry: one effect, no plaintext retention/replay or automatic replacement.
A21.observation: Concurrent transactional service requests and sequential browser replays exercised the issuance ledger. The browser checked that the secret did not appear after leaving the result.
A21.remaining: Inject an issuance rollback and lost commit response at the HTTP boundary and verify expiration and normal refresh on both issuance types.

A22.criteria: Two DIFFERENT recovery-generation intents/tabs: expected-set conflict prevents silent invalidation of the first generated set; replacement requires new explicit confirmation.
A22.observation: ConcurrentIssuanceAndRecoveryGenerationRejectReplayAndStaleSets exercised different intents and rejected the stale generation.

A23.criteria: Secret-page normal refresh and Back/Forward cache; page departure versus simple focus loss; clipboard denied/unavailable: no reissuance or secret resurrection, useful copy fallback, no premature secret loss.
A23.observation: Page-departure and clipboard fallback logic exists. Guide screenshots redact one-time values before capture.
A23.remaining: Actual BFCache restore, focus-only loss and denied clipboard need full browser evidence.

A24.criteria: Recovery preparation, replace, code use, invalid/consumed/expired/cross-account cases and atomic reset: can recover without the missing passkey; documented effects and fresh enrollment correct.
A24.observation: Browser profiles used a code without the old passkey, denied anonymous use and replay, revoked the old DAV/OAuth grants, and reenrolled. Transactional integration covered replacement of the existing set, invalid and cross-account secrets, expiration and rollback. Offline local and external recovery also ran.

A25.criteria: Password change, current/other-session revocation, application-password/grant revocation and identity linking: specific confirmations and existing revocation semantics retained.
A25.observation: Typed Security actions render named reviews and preserve account-generation invalidation.
A25.remaining: Run every named revocation, password and identity-linking workflow with an actual browser and verify the current and other session effects.

A26.criteria: Empty export for all three types and a content-change race: no false download success, neutral correct guidance and authorization before revealing emptiness.
A26.observation: The revised empty Task list returns neutral resource-specific feedback and no download.
A26.remaining: Run the same case for Calendars and Journals, including the race after authorized admission.

A27.criteria: Populated imports/exports for all three types, duplicate UID/conflict/wrong type/malformed/zero-ready data: accurate previews, preserved data/format, no unsupported overwrite.
A27.observation: HTTP import/export tests exercised conflicts, malformed input, denied destinations, preserved bytes and native fixtures. Browser evidence includes a populated Journal with a GET import result.

A28.criteria: Preview/confirm PRG, report paging, preview replacement, stale auth, expired token, revoked access, known rollback, uncertain result/restart: correct stage identity/lifetime and no duplicate/partial import.
A28.observation: The revised browser follows preview and confirm to GET reports. HTTP and staging tests exercised paging, preview replacement, stale authority, expiry, concurrent confirmation and rollback. The proxy profile interrupted a real transaction, restarted, rejected the old preview and imported from a fresh preview.

A29.criteria: Maximum-size/overlapping/capacity/disk-exhaustion/crash cases required by the existing portability gates: resource budget, private permissions, cleanup, retry and immutable source data remain correct.
A29.observation: HTTP capacity and upload checks exercised real byte limits. The proxy fixture interrupted a transaction and checked rollback, restart and a fresh import.
A29.remaining: Run an independent filesystem-full scenario and verify cleanup and retry on a dedicated volume.

A30.criteria: Account creation/handoff/errors, status+method filters and disabled/external accounts: truthful instructions, no plaintext success data, no unimplemented temporary-password claim.
A30.observation: Account creation, safe handoff, combinations of directory status and identity method, and separation of managed and local accounts ran across the browser and HTTP suites.

A31.criteria: Self-disable/last-admin disable and concurrent opposing administrator disable requests: browser path preserves at least one enabled administrator; valid other-account disable still revokes access and retains content; offline recovery unaffected.
A31.observation: OpposingBrowserDisablesKeepAnEnabledAdministrator exercised concurrent administrators. Offline recovery ran in its own extracted fixture.

A32.criteria: Group create/rename/member selection/add/remove/delete: exact consequences, bounded authorized lookup, conflicts/limits and privacy. Rename does not change sync; membership does reconcile correctly.
A32.observation: The maintained browser profile exercised group creation, validation, rename, membership add/remove, named group deletion and overlapping grants. The HTTP suite exercised bounded capacity, reconciliation, disabled membership and rejection of a stale grant review at the same count.

A33.criteria: Audit mapping for all/unknown/historical/deleted targets, current-name joins, XSS, filter/paging, pruning and audit-failure rollback: IDs preserved, no expanded sensitive persistence.
A33.observation: Audit page uses human labels, current names where available and technical details. Audit pruning and transactional rollback tests ran.
A33.remaining: Verify every historical/unknown/deleted category and filtering and pagination edge case in the revised view.

A34.criteria: Native-app registration invalid fields/cancel/remove: editable form and named server-wide effect; full grant revocation atomic; OAuth protocol/security regression gates unchanged.
A34.observation: The final extracted /team fixture exercised invalid redirect recovery with an associated field error, cancellation, and named application removal. OAuth HTTP and storage tests exercised atomic removal with active grants and in-flight exchanges and refreshes.

A35.criteria: Diagnostics root/subpath/local origin, spoofed forwarding headers, database outage, metrics windows and bounded problem buffer: honest labels, no secrets/private paths or invented health.
A35.observation: Diagnostics were rendered for root and /team and security/diagnostics tests checked real origin and bounded request records.
A35.remaining: Verify history windows and database outage against the exact extracted proxy fixture.

A36.criteria: Every primary journey with keyboard, accessible form/status/focus behavior, screen reader where available, 320px/390px/desktop, zoom/text resizing, light/dark, forced colors and reduced motion.
A36.observation: Keyboard menu opening and Escape/focus, 320px/390px/desktop, dark, forced colors and reduced motion were exercised.
A36.remaining: Manual keyboard coverage of every primary task, screen reader announcements, browser zoom/text sizing and the actual passkey provider remain.

A37.criteria: New and upgraded schema, current restore invalidation, durable issuance intents, pending-flow cleanup and backup/restore: new persistence cannot revive old browser authority/credentials.
A37.observation: Fresh V18 and V9/V17 migrations, journal preservation and closed initialization were tested. Restoring a real pending issuance row cleared it and invalidated old credentials.

A38.criteria: Complete final guide/images/links/anchors/package; source-free extracted-bundle walkthrough; actual client content round trip; final manual acceptance fixture and truthful remaining gates.
A38.observation: Validated guide links, anchors and 27 reviewed captures, built the unpublished archive, walked through extracted root and /team installs, completed independent client content operations, and verified a fresh uninitialized manual fixture. The receipt marks manual testing pending.
